title: Bonyas ben Bonyas
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Eruvin 85b: he came before Rabbi, who said to them, “Make room for a hundred-year-old man.” Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yose said to him: “Rabbi, this man’s father has a thousand ships at sea and correspondingly a thousand towns on land.” Rabbi said to him: “When you reach this man’s father, tell him not to send him before me in these garments.” The Arukh, entry סבן, reads ben Nannas; Rashi wrote that some read that he was Rabbi’s student. In Eruvin 83a: “When Rav Dimi came, he said: Bonyos sent Rabbi a modius of kondeis from Na’usa”; Dikdukei Soferim reads ben Bonyas. In Gittin 59a, Bonyas ben Bonyas sent Rabbi precious linen garments, and Rashi explains: he was a wealthy Jew.

notes.text: קונדיס is kept as kondeis, not mustard; saved Davidson English Eruvin83a interprets a measure. Supplied בן מאה שנה says a hundred-year-old man; saved Davidson85b has בן מאה מנה, worth a hundred maneh. These competing readings are disclosed rather than silently replacing Hyman with the digital witness.

The consulted Eruvin 85b gives ben Bonyas and a hundred maneh, while Hyman supplies a hundred-year-old man. The passage continues into 86a with a second visitor worth two hundred maneh before the father’s ships, towns and garments exchange. Hyman’s compressed sequence is retained without identifying the two visitors. Eruvin 83a treats kondeis as part of a measure, not mustard. Exact Arukh, Rashi-student and Dikdukei Soferim readings remain Hyman’s reports.
